title: vc-issuer: revoke() swallows a failed DB UPDATE — the route answers 200, the row stays unrevoked, and a restart reloads it as valid
description:
**BLUF:** In vc-issuer, `credentialRepo.revoke()` swallows a failed database UPDATE and keeps the revoke only in memory: the route `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke` answers 200 "revoked successfully", the database row stays UNrevoked, and after a restart `loadFromDb` loads it unrevoked, so the credential verifies as valid. Measured by gate 152 for an ordinary Error (its scenario C); the restart is read, not run. Pre-existing, not introduced by pull request 1968 ([https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1968](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1968>)); found by gate 152. Same fail-open family as KS-1958.

## What happens

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`: when `revoke()`'s database UPDATE fails, the error is swallowed ("kept in memory"). The credential is revoked in this process's memory only.
* The route answers 200 "revoked successfully" although the database row is unchanged.
* After a restart, `loadFromDb` (the only place memory is filled from the database) loads the row unrevoked, and the credential verifies as valid (read, not run past the restart).

## Measured (gate 152, scenario C)

The real route and repository were run; only `../db` (an in-memory fake table that can fail its UPDATE) and the logger were replaced. With an ordinary Error on the UPDATE: the route answers 200 "revoked successfully", memory is revoked, the database row is not. Base and head (pull request 1968) behave the same.

## A hostile value at the same place (finding G152-F4, read from source and measured for revoke)

For a revoked Proxy or an Error with a throwing `message` getter on that UPDATE, the revoke answers 500 after memory is already revoked, because `revoke()`'s own catch (around line 502) still reads `err?.message` unguarded. Three sibling catches in the same file still do too: `store` (around line 98), `getReadableByHash` (around 324, the by-hash route's path) and `selectList` (around 413, the list route); `db.ts` `probeDb` as well. Those belong to the KS-1868 site list.

## Fix class

Not chosen by the gate. A revoke that cannot reach the database should not answer success; how it should behave (refuse and leave memory unrevoked, or accept and retry) is the same availability-against-fail-closed ruling as KS-1958.

## Limits

Not tested: a real restart, a real Postgres, the revoke route over HTTP beyond the route dispatch used by the sibling suites, Node 24. Related, not the same defect: KS-1295 (`store()` falls back to memory silently), KS-1684 (the creator refused on the memory fallback after a revoke), KS-1899 (`revoke()` has no ownership check of its own).

nodes.title: Refs KS-1959: a revoke whose database write does not take effect answers 503, not success

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** At develop `5fc5569ed96a`, four catch sites that this ticket's "A hostile value at the same place" section names still read `err?.message` unguarded: `store` (line 98), `getReadableByHash` (line 370), `selectList` (line 459) and `probeDb` (line 102 of the db file). The revoke catch is guarded since PR 2005. Gate 191 measured one of the four: `GET /api/credentials/by-hash/:hash` answers HTTP 500 when the database read throws a revoked Proxy or an Error whose `message` getter throws (3 cells, the same at base and head of PR 2003). The ticket's "around 324 / 413 / 502" are gate 152's numbers at PR 1968's base; the tip's are below.

Source: gate 191 verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate191-ks1958-pr2003/verdict.md` lines 27 to 29 (G191-F3, LOW, pre-existing); gate 152 verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-03_gate152-ks1868-pr1968/verdict.md` line 71 (G152-F4, graded there "recommended follow-up, read from source", no severity letter); gate 194 verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-05_gate194-ks1959/verdict.md` line 106 (the revoke catch rewritten with a guard). Product code read by the filing seat at develop `5fc5569ed96ac61f64823cc9e1fa841899aa1f62` (the PR 2006 squash) through the GitHub contents API, not run.

Lines as read at that sha:
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`: the `store` catch opens at 95 and reads `error: err?.message` at 98 (log text "DB write failed for credential — kept in memory"); the `getReadableByHash` catch opens at 369 and reads at 370 (log text "DB hash lookup failed — falling back to memory"); the `selectList` catch opens at 458 and reads at 459 (log text "DB list failed — falling back to memory").
* Routes into them, in `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts`: the by-hash handler (`router.get('/by-hash/:hash'` at line 402) calls `getReadableByHash` at 409; the list handler (`router.get('/'` at 236) calls `listReadable` at 246, which reaches `selectList` at line 335 of the repository file (`list` reaches it at 280); issuance (`router.post('/'` at 146) calls `store` at 210.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/vc-issuer/src/db.ts`: `probeDb` (line 95) returns `error: err?.message` at line 102, in a catch that opens at 100.
* Guarded at the same sha, for contrast: lines 49, 162, 215, 250 and 567 of the repository file each read the value inside an inner try; the `revoke` catch at 564 is the PR 2005 form.

Measured (gate 191, G191-F3): `getReadableByHash`'s catch reads `err?.message` unguarded; a revoked Proxy and a throwing getter give HTTP 500, an ordinary Error gives 200 from memory, and the 500 body carries no planted text. The same 3 of 3 outcomes at base and head. 3 cells, both sides, matrix harness Q4 cells.

Not measured: anything by the filing seat (nothing was run). `store`, `selectList` and `probeDb` were read from source by gate 152 and have not been driven with a hostile value by any gate; whether `GET /api/credentials` answers 500 the way the by-hash route does; whether any running stack or box differs from the source read; what a restart changes.

**BLUF:** Deployed, behaviour not run: PR 2005 (17abf8ee98a5) is live on kintsugi and demo at develop 07a2d62be6a0 (fix strings live: 2 of 2 on demo; F2 and F3 on kintsugi); not closed because the 503 path is POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke with a failing database write, which is authenticated, audited and needs fault injection.

Source: Seat D 53rd (kintsugi) `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatD-53rd/evidence/F6_ticket_table.tsv` line 4 and `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatD-53rd/HANDOVER.md` line 4; Seat D 52nd (demo) `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatD-52nd/evidence/F6_ticket_table.tsv` line 42 and `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatD-52nd/HANDOVER.md` lines 4 and 28; PR facts read from GitHub.

Rows as written. Seat D 53rd, line 4: "KS-1959 | 2005 | 17abf8ee98a5 | DEPLOYED; behaviour NOT-RUN | vc-issuer 1fc1b18f7b28; F2, F3 ADD 0->1 live. The 503 path is POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke with a failing DB write: authenticated, audited (middleware/audit.ts:25,58), and needs fault injection". Seat D 52nd, line 42: "KS-1959 In Progress fix strings live 2 of 2" (demo).

* PR 2005 merged 2026-11-04T22:55:11Z, merge_commit_sha 17abf8ee98a50c609de42d54d4f8c8d7aad156eb, base develop. It is an ancestor of 07a2d62be6a0 (git merge-base --is-ancestor, rc 0). Both boxes run 07a2d62be6a0 (Seat D 53rd HANDOVER line 4 for kintsugi, Seat D 52nd HANDOVER line 4 for demo).

Not measured:
* The 503 itself: no failing database write was induced and no authenticated revoke call was made, on either box.
* Kintsugi's fix-string count beyond F2 and F3 as the row states them.

**BLUF:** PR 2005, head a968818a0038, ready for gate.

https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2005 (Refs KS-1959). A revoke whose database write does not take effect now answers 503 instead of 200; verify is unchanged. Tier-1 gate next; no state change made here.
